text.tspan: Materialise (file) — deferred: nothing is sent here
(FUSE: create)
Materialise (directory) — straight to the server
(FUSE: mkdir)
Remove — one script for both
(FUSE: unlink, rmdir)
DbWrite insert a local node
no file id yet — that is what marks it
as not yet materialised on the server
invalidate in-flight listings
a new child must survive a PROPFIND
that was already on its way
register it dirty
A new file is a pending change even with no bytes,
so touch still creates it. Created and deleted before
any flush — an editor probe, a temp file — and the
server never hears about it

g.text: an ephemeral editor or office file?

text.tspan: keep it local-only
no upload on flush, no DELETE on remove:
fewer round-trips, and it dodges server quirks
DbWrite reconcile_children
the new directory arrives with its server ids
DbRead resolve the child by name
The kernel names (parent, name), never an identity,
so the script starts by finding out which object it
is about to remove
does it exist on the server?
(a deferred create never got a file id)
Net DELETE
recursive for a directory
FileIo drop the buffer
forget the pending mtime and the ignored mark
DbRead / DbWrite drop the pins this subtree carried,
and the eviction markers beside its blobs.
A leftover pin marker is not untidy but harmful: those
bytes stay exempt from the cache budget forever, and a
later file handed the same id inherits the protection
invalidate in-flight listings
a PROPFIND already on its way must not re-add it
A running upload of this file is let finish first —
it may already have landed, and the DELETE has to
apply to what is really there.
A background hydration for a pin is aborted instead:
the file is gone, so the rest of the download is waste
